intro: Accountants build complex problem solving, judgment and persuasion skills that open doors well beyond tax season. The strongest matches among the 25 careers below are Treasurers and Controllers and Financial Managers, both at 92%.
why_it_works: Accounting trains you to spot errors, explain numbers to people who are not experts and make calls that affect a whole budget. Finance management, analysis and compliance roles rate those same abilities highly in O*NET. Management Analysts, for example, use the problem solving you apply to reconciliations to fix how a company runs. Because most of these roles sit in the same business world, your degree usually still counts. The skills to strengthen are operations analysis and systems evaluation.
tips: Use your industry knowledge: an accountant at a hospital or software firm has an edge in that sector's finance and analyst roles.
Add one analytics skill, such as SQL or a business intelligence tool, to move toward analyst and controller work.
Talk to the finance leaders you already report numbers to; many controller and analyst hires come from inside.

faq.q: What can accountants do besides accounting?
faq.a: The closest matches are Treasurers and Controllers (92%), Financial Managers (92%) and Compensation, Benefits, and Job Analysis Specialists (86%), based on O*NET 31.0. Management Analysts (84%) and Actuaries (82%) are also close, and they put your analytical skills to work outside traditional accounting.

faq.q: Which careers for accountants pay more?
faq.a: 9 of the 25 matches pay more than the $83,680 median for accountants and auditors. Financial Managers earn a median of $166,570, a 99% increase, Actuaries earn $130,000 (+55%) and Management Analysts earn $101,860 (+22%), according to BLS May 2025 data.

faq.q: Do accountants need more school to change careers?
faq.a: Rarely. 24 of the 25 matches usually need no more education than an accountant has, based on O*NET Job Zones, and only 1 usually needs a graduate degree. The bigger step is experience: finance manager roles often go to people who have led teams or budgets.

faq.q: What jobs are similar to accounting?
faq.a: Inside the same field, Financial Examiners (93%), Budget Analysts (92%) and Credit Analysts (91%) are the nearest roles. They use the same review and reporting skills but focus on regulation, public budgets or lending decisions instead of keeping the books.
